title: Olivia Wilde's New Movie 'The Invite' Is the Talk of the Town!
summary: Have you ever thrown a party and worried no one would show up? Well, Olivia Wilde's new movie "The Invite" had the opposite problem! It opened in only seven theaters last weekend, but it still made a whopping $393,357. That's like each theater selling out a huge concert hall! On average, each screen earned $56,194. That's a lot of popcorn. This is called a "platform release," when a movie starts small before going big. The studio, A24, is known for this. They bought "The Invite" after a big bidding war at the Sundance Film Festival. Compared to other A24 movies, "The Invite" is doing great. It almost matched the opening of "The Moment" with Charli XCX, which made $427,000 but on only four screens. And it's way ahead of "Mother Mary," which averaged only $33,000 per screen. The all-time champ for A24 platform openings is "Marty Supreme," which made $863,000 from just six screens! Other indie movies are also having fun. "Maddie's Secret" and "Rose of Nevada" are still going strong. A new drama from Spain called "Romeria" made $15,193. And an Italian film, "For the Love of a Woman," brought in $4,294. Even an older movie, "Blue Heron," crept back into the top 10 after 11 weeks! It's almost at $600,000 total. So, if you see "The Invite" pop up at a theater near you, grab a ticket. It's the hottest party in town!
why_it_matters: This shows how something small can become a big deal—like when a new game or trend starts with just a few kids at school before everyone joins in. Patience can build more excitement!

background_read: A24 is a movie studio known for making and releasing independent films that often get a lot of attention, like 'Everything Everywhere All at Once'.
The Sundance Film Festival happens every year in Utah and is where many small movies are first shown and where studios fight to buy them—called a bidding war.
A platform release helps build excitement: a movie starts in a few big cities, gets good reviews, and then more people want to see it when it comes to their town.
Article_Structure: WHO: Olivia Wilde's new movie 'The Invite' and studio A24.
WHAT: The movie had a huge opening weekend even though it was shown in only seven theaters, earning a lot of money per screen.
WHERE: The theaters were in the U.S., part of a small release before going nationwide.
WHY: The platform release strategy and the studio's reputation helped make the movie a hot ticket, and the article compares its success to other indie films.

perspectives.description: The movie's success proves that independent films can attract huge crowds and make a lot of money per screen, which encourages studios to take risks on unique stories.
A limited opening means not everyone can see it right away, and some fans in small towns might feel left out or have to wait a long time.
Comparing different platform releases helps us understand what strategies work, but every movie is different and numbers alone don't always tell the full story.
